record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Determine all pairs {p, q}, with p and q in {3, 4, ...} ∪ {∞}, for which there exist infinite chiral maps, equivalently infinite chiral polyhedra, of Schläfli type {p, q}.

evidence.quote: Problem 21 Determine all pairs {p, q} with p, q ∈ {3, 4, . . . } ∪ {∞} for which there exist infinite chiral maps (polyhedra) with Schlafli type {p, q}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A map is a 2-cell embedding of a connected graph into a surface (without boundary). A map is of Schläfli type {p,q} (with p,q ∈ {3,4,5,...} ∪ {∞}) if every face is a p-gon (a ∞-gon being an infinite-sided face) and every vertex has valency q. The automorphism group of a map acts freely on its flags (incident vertex–edge–face triples). A map is called regular if its automorphism group is transitive on flags, and chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags such that adjacent flags always lie in different orbits (equivalently, the map admits all rotational symmetries about faces and vertices but no reflective symmetries). Such maps are equivalently described as abstract polyhedra (rank-3 abstract polytopes) that are chiral.

Determine the set of all pairs {p,q} with p,q ∈ {3,4,5,...} ∪ {∞} for which there exists an infinite chiral map (equivalently, an infinite chiral abstract polyhedron) of Schläfli type {p,q}.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on chiral maps and polytopes (including work on tight chiral polyhedra and on infinite regular/chiral maps and the surfaces they live on) addresses partial cases (e.g., type {4,4}, tight chiral polyhedra, existence on the Loch Ness monster surface), but no source provides a complete determination of all pairs {p,q} ∈ ({3,4,...} ∪ {∞})² for which an infinite chiral map of type {p,q} exists. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On infinite regular and chiral maps
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that infinite regular and chiral maps take place on surfaces with at most one end... an infinite regular or chiral map on an orientable surface with genus can only be realized on the Loch Ness monster.
status_evidence.claim: Provides structural results on the surfaces supporting infinite chiral maps but does not classify the Schläfli types {p,q} that arise.

status_evidence.title: Tight chiral polyhedra
status_evidence.snippet: Schläfli symbols of tight chiral polyhedra have been fully characterized.
status_evidence.claim: Only the restricted 'tight' subclass of chiral polyhedra has its Schläfli types fully characterized; the general case is not.

status_evidence.title: On the Schläfli symbol of chiral extensions of polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses which Schläfli symbols can occur for chiral extensions of polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent work continues on which Schläfli symbols are realized by chiral polytopes, indicating the general problem remains unsettled.
